extracted.intended_audience: individual customs brokers, brokerages/employers of brokers, prospective accreditors and training providers, and CBP compliance/regulatory staff
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and administrative framework establishing mandatory continuing broker education for individual customs brokers (36 credits per triennial period), accreditation of courses, recordkeeping, reporting, and enforcement (suspension/revocation) procedures under 19 CFR part 111.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing broker education requirement (definition and purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Continuing broker education requirement" means an individual broker's obligation to complete a certain number of continuing education credits of qualifying continuing broker education, as set forth in subpart F of this part, in order to maintain sufficient knowledge of customs and related laws, regulations, and procedures, bookkeeping, accounting, and all other appropriate matters necessary to render valuable service to importers and drawback claimants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the purpose: maintain sufficient knowledge of customs-related matters; applies to individual brokers and is administered under Subpart F (§§111.101–111.104).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required minimum number of continuing education credits
rubrics_metrics.description: All individual brokers who are subject to the continuing broker education requirement must complete at least 36 continuing education credits of qualifying continuing broker education each triennial period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 36-credit requirement is the chosen alternative (Alternative 2). Upon reinstatement after voluntary suspension, credits are prorated at one continuing education credit for each complete remaining month until the end of the triennial period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to the continuing education requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual brokers are excepted from the continuing broker education requirement during a period of voluntary suspension (§111.52) or when they have not held their license for an entire triennial period at the time of the status report submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement after voluntary suspension triggers prorated credit calculation (one credit per complete remaining month).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting requirement (status report certification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual brokers subject to the requirement must report and certify their compliance upon submission of the triennial status report required under §111.30(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Status reports are the mechanism for certification; failure to report/certify triggers CBP notification and potential enforcement (see §111.104).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping requirements (what to retain and retention period)
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual brokers must retain, for three years following the submission of the status report, information and documentation for qualifying continuing education completed during a triennial period, including: title of course, provider/host name, dates attended, number of credits accrued, location, and any documentation evidencing registration/attendance/completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records must be made available to CBP on request within 30 calendar days; CBP may request in-person inspection or delivery by hard-copy, electronic means, or combination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of continuing education credit (unit and calculation)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Continuing education credit" means the unit of measurement used for meeting the continuing broker education requirement. The smallest recognized unit is half of one continuing education credit, which requires 30 minutes of continuous participation in qualifying continuing continuing broker education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For qualifying activities lasting more than 30 minutes, half of one credit may be claimed for every full 30 minutes thereafter. Examples: qualifying activity >60 and <90 minutes = 1 credit; activity lasting 90 minutes = 1.5 credits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifying continuing broker education (general definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Qualifying continuing broker education" means any training or educational activity that is eligible or, if required, has been approved for continuing education credit, in accordance with §111.103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The specific qualifying types and provider rules are set out in §111.103 (see separate metrics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Providers of qualifying continuing broker education (government vs. other)
rubrics_metrics.description: Training offered by CBP or another U.S. government agency (online or in-person) constitutes qualifying continuing broker education if content is relevant to customs business. Any other training not offered by a U.S. government agency will not be qualifying unless approved for credit by a CBP-selected accreditor before the activity is provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government-offered trainings do not require accreditation. Non-government providers must obtain prior accreditation approval for the specific activity to be qualifying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognized types of trainings/educational activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualifying activities must be one of: (i) a seminar, webinar, or workshop (online or in-person, live or recorded) conducted by an instructor/discussion leader/speaker; (ii) a symposium or convention (except FACA meetings); (iii) online self-guided coursework/workshop/module culminating in a retention test; (iv) preparation of subject matter for presentation; or (v) presentation of subject matter as instructor/discussion leader/speaker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each listed type is eligible if it meets provider/accreditation rules. Attendance at FACA meetings is explicitly excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special allowance for instructors, discussion leaders, and speakers
rubrics_metrics.description: Contingent upon the approval by a CBP-selected accreditor, an individual broker may claim half of one credit for each full 30 minutes spent presenting subject matter or preparing subject matter for presentation at qualifying training activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval by a CBP-selected accreditor is required regardless of whether the activity is offered by a government agency or other provider.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on instructor/presenter credit claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Limitations: (i) For any session presented at one time, an individual broker may claim at most one continuing education credit for time spent preparing subject matter for that single presentation; (ii) per triennial period, an individual broker may claim at most a combined total of 12 continuing education credits earned for presenting and preparing subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These caps apply in addition to obtaining accreditor approval to claim such credits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to obtain accreditor approval to claim instructor credits
rubrics_metrics.description: Regardless of whether the training is offered by a U.S. government agency or another provider, any instructor/discussion leader/speaker seeking to claim continuing education credit under the instructor allowance must obtain the approval of a CBP-selected accreditor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even government-offered trainings require accreditor approval for instructor/preparer credit claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of accreditors (process and publication of criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Trade will select accreditors based on an RFI and RFP announced through SAM (or other approved system) in accordance with the FAR. The Executive Assistant Commissioner, Office of Trade, will periodically publish Federal Register notices announcing the criteria CBP will use to select an accreditor, the application periods, and the period of award for a CBP-selected accreditor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection uses standard federal procurement notice processes (SAM, RFI/RFP, FAR compliance); criteria and windows will be publicly announced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibilities and rules for CBP-selected accreditors
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP-selected accreditors administer accreditation for non-government trainings by reviewing and approving or denying such content for continuing education credit. An approval is valid for one year and may be renewed; accreditors will not deny review or approval solely because a content was previously denied by any CBP-selected accreditor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accreditors act as third-party reviewers; approval validity and renewal process described; fairness provision prevents denial solely for prior denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on self-certification by accreditors
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP-selected accreditors may not approve their own trainings or educational activities for continuing education credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents conflict of interest — accreditors cannot accredit their own offerings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to report/certify compliance — notification and corrective actions
rubrics_metrics.description: If an individual broker submits the status report but fails to report and certify compliance, CBP will notify the individual broker of the failure. Upon notification, the broker must within 30 calendar days either submit a corrected status report reflecting compliance (if credits already completed) or complete the required credits and submit a corrected status report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification will be sent to CBP's address on record or electronically; corrected report or completion must be done on or before 30 calendar days from notice issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement — suspension for failure to correct within 30 days
rubrics_metrics.description: If the individual broker does not take the corrective actions described within 30 calendar days from CBP's notification, CBP will take actions to suspend the broker's license in accordance with subpart D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension is the immediate enforcement mechanism for noncompliance with reporting/certification after notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement — revocation for failure to correct within 120 days after suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If the broker's license has been suspended and the broker fails to take the corrective actions on or before 120 calendar days from the issuance date of the order of suspension, CBP will take actions to revoke the broker's license (without prejudice to filing for a new license).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revocation follows prolonged failure to remedy after suspension; revocation is without prejudice to a new application per subpart D.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triennial period definition
rubrics_metrics.description: "Triennial period" means a period of three years commencing on February 1, 1985, or on February 1 in any third year thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to calculate the 36-credit requirement and proration on reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status report content requirements for individual brokers (§111.30(d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each individual broker must state in the status report whether actively engaged in transacting business as a broker. If active, the broker must also state business name/address and email (for sole proprietors), employer name/address (if employed), whether they meet applicable requirements of §§111.11 and 111.19 and have not engaged in conduct that could be grounds for suspension/revocation under §111.53, and report and certify compliance with the continuing education requirement. If not active, the broker must provide current mailing address/email, the statements about meeting applicable requirements and conduct, and report and certify compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Status report is the vehicle for multiple certifications including continuing education compliance and fitness to practice; employers that are partnerships/associations/corporations have different reporting rules (see §111.30).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accreditation approval validity and renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: A CBP-selected accreditor's approval of a training or educational activity for continuing education credit is valid for one year and the accreditation may be renewed through any CBP-selected accreditor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approvals are time-limited to one year; renewal can be done via any CBP-selected accreditor (not necessarily the original).

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) compliance and information collection requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections of information under these regulations are provided for by OMB control number 1651-0034; the addition of self-attestation and submission of records will add about 30–45 minutes (0.5–0.75 hours) per respondent. Estimated time per response is 31.5 minutes (0.525 hours), estimated total annual burden hours 2,442, and estimated number of respondents 13,952.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An agency may not conduct or require a person to respond to information collection without a valid OMB control number; CBP will submit adjustments to OMB to account for these changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act / small-entity impact criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Small business within the Freight Transportation Arrangement Industry is defined as a firm with annual receipts less than $20.0 million (2022 dollars). CBP generally considers effects of 1 percent or less of annual receipts not to be a significant impact for purposes of the Regulatory Flexibility Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP estimated average annualized cost per affected firm (~$6,663; about 0.3% of receipts) and therefore certified the rule does not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accreditor review fairness (no denial solely for prior denial)
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP-selected accreditors will not deny review or approval of a training or educational activity for continuing education credit solely because it was previously denied by the CBP-selected accreditor or any other CBP-selected accreditor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures applicants can obtain a fresh review and reduces risk of absolute gatekeeping by one accreditor.
